rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing and use of algorithmic devices (automated rent-pricing software) by landlords and apartment owners to set rents in Santa Ana.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and apartment owners of residential rental property in Santa Ana; also sellers and licensors of algorithmic devices.
rules.penalty: Fine of $1,000; enforced mainly through the city's existing code enforcement system.
rules.citation: Santa Ana ordinance prohibiting algorithmic devices (2026; municipal code citation not given in source)
rules.quoted_span: “The purpose and intent of this [ordinance] is to protect the residents of Santa Ana from artificially inflated rental rates and unfair rent increases by prohibiting the sale, licensing and use of Algorithmic Devices,” according to a staff report.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary news source; no ordinance number or municipal code section given. First reading Feb. 17, 2026; final adoption at a Tuesday meeting shortly before the March 9, 2026 article (likely March 3, 2026). Article says the final vote put the ordinance into effect, but California city ordinances generally take effect 30 days after adoption, so effective date may be early April 2026. Industry group suggests potential legal liability/possible interplay with recently adopted state regulations.
